caption:
🚆 Germany vs Poland — every train of the same day, Thursday 15 October 2026.

Same rules on both sides: long-distance and regional trains only, without Germany's S-Bahn or the urban SKM lines of Warsaw, Gdańsk and Kraków. Germany ran over 26,000 trains that day, Poland about 6,000, on a territory only 12% smaller. Long-distance trains (EIP, EIC, IC, TLK) make up 9% of Polish traffic against 3% in Germany, and Poland's busiest moment comes in the afternoon (650 trains on the move at 16:45), not at the morning rush.

📊 Data: DELFI e.V. via gtfs.de (CC BY 4.0) · PKP PLK & Koleje Mazowieckie data, GTFS by Mikołaj Kuranowski. Trains follow the real tracks (© OpenStreetMap); positions interpolated between stops.
🌍 Relief: AWS Terrain Tiles · Natural Earth.
